name: prose-4k-1
input:
Here are some notes I have been collecting, just for background mood and vocabulary.

- **No scope sprawl.** Text LLM inference first. No image, audio or 3D (mlx-serve's burden). Vision encoders are a later block type, not a side product.
- **No kernel enters without passing its reference test.** sm_121 CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE emitting `!!!!!` and a cuDNN FP8 GEMM hanging after 250k steps were both shipped by others.

---

## 1. Language and build

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Host: server, scheduler, KV manager, loaders, metrics, UI server, CLI | **Rust** (stable, edition 2021) | Native speed and startup with memory safety; best ecosystem for this exact stack: `tokenizers` (HF), `safetensors`, `minijinja` (HF chat templates), `llguidance` (structured output), `axum`/`tokio`, `ratatui`, `prometheus-client`, `opentelemetry`, `cudarc` (CUDA driver + NCCL). One static binary per platform. |
| GPU kernels, NVIDIA | **CUDA C++** (+ inline PTX where profiling demands), AOT-compiled to fatbins for `sm_121` (GB10), plus `sm_90/100/120` when hardware appears | Cold JIT compiles take minutes on GB10; AOT removes that. |
| GPU kernels, AMD | **HIP C++** (+ inline GCN/RDNA asm where needed), AOT for `gfx1201` | Same as radiance, which holds the R9700 bar. |
| Shared kernel code | One `ik_portable.h` header that maps CUDA/HIP intrinsics; elementwise, norm, rope, sampling and quant-pack kernels compile from one source for both | Halves the simple-kernel work. GEMM and attention stay arch-specific. |
| Apple (dev) / Arc (later) | Metal / Vulkan or SYCL backends behind the same trait | Not built now; the trait is shaped so they slot in. |
| Offline tools | Python (uv), never imported by the server | Golden logits via HF `transformers`, plotting, converters. |

Rejected: C++ host (radiance proves it works, but modularity, packaging and the server/UI ecosystem are slower to build); Zig host (mlx-serve proves it works, but the ML-adjacent library ecosystem is thin; no `tokenizers`/`llguidance` equivalents); Python host (per-step overhead, startup, container weight); Mojo (tried in `TensorFold-mojo*`, not merged). Assembly is used per hot spot, not as a language choice.


**Status (section 1).**

| Claim | Status | Evidence on origin/main |
|---|---|---|
| Rust host, one binary per platform | **implemented** | [`Cargo.toml`](../Cargo.toml) workspace, edition 2021, `rust-toolchain.toml` pins 1.90.0 |
| Host crates `tokenizers`, `minijinja`, `llguidance`, `axum`, `ratatui` | **implemented** | [`Cargo.toml`](../Cargo.toml) dependencies |
| Host crates `prometheus-client`, `opentelemetry`, `cudarc`, `rust-embed` | **planned** | not in `Cargo.toml`: metrics are hand-written ([`crates/intarsia-server/src/metrics.rs`](../crates/intarsia-server/src/metrics.rs)), CUDA is bound through own FFI ([`crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/src/ffi.rs`](../crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/src/ffi.rs)), UI files are `include_str!`d ([`crates/intarsia-ui/src/lib.rs`](../crates/intarsia-ui/src/lib.rs)) |
| CUDA C++ AOT for `sm_121` | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/build.rs`](../crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/build.rs) (default `sm_121`) |
| HIP C++ AOT for `gfx1201` | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-backend-hip/build.rs`](../crates/intarsia-backend-hip/build.rs) (default `gfx1201`) |
| One `ik_portable.h` so simple kernels compile from one source for CUDA and HIP | **partial** | [`kernels/common/ik_portable.h`](../kernels/common/ik_portable.h) exists, but `kernels/cuda/*.cu` and `kernels/hip/*.hip` are separate files |
| Apple (dev) / Arc (later): Metal / Vulkan or SYCL behind the same trait | **partial** | Metal **implemented**: [`crates/intarsia-backend-metal/src/lib.rs`](../crates/intarsia-backend-metal/src/lib.rs); Vulkan/SYCL **planned**: no code |
| Offline Python tools, never imported by the server | **implemented** | [`tools/golden.py`](../tools/golden.py), [`tools/scribe.py`](../tools/scribe.py) |

---

## 2. System overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Front["Front door (crate: intarsia-server)"]
    OAI["OpenAI: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/models"]
    ANT["Anthropic: /v1/messages"]
    UI["Embedded web UI: chat, live dashboard, live architecture map"]
    MET["/metrics (Prometheus), OTLP, /events (SSE)"]
  end
  subgraph Core["Engine core (crate: intarsia-core)"]
    TOK["Tokenizer + chat template + parsers (tools, reasoning)"]
    SCH["Scheduler: continuous batching, chunked prefill, priorities"]
    KV["KV manager: paged blocks, radix prefix cache, host tier"]
    SPEC["Speculation: MTP, DFlash-style drafter, n-gram"]
    SMP["Sampler + structured output (llguidance)"]
    PLAN["Plan compiler: recipe → op graph → kernel selection → captured graphs per batch bucket"]
  end
  subgraph Pieces["Pieces (plugins)"]
    REC["Recipes (TOML)"]
    BLK["Block library: attention (GQA/MLA/SWA/GDN), FFN (dense/MoE), norms, rope"]
    QF["Quant formats: BF16, FP8, NVFP4, MXFP4, GGUF k-quants, EXL3, AWQ/GPTQ"]
    KR["Kernel registry: (op, backend, arch, dtype/quant, shape class) → impl + reference + autotune DB"]
    BEN["Bench plugins: micro, e2e, localeval"]
  end
  subgraph HW["Backends (crate: intarsia-backend-*)"]
    CPU["cpu-ref (always on: the oracle)"]
    CUDA["cuda (GB10 sm_121)"]
    HIP["hip (R9700 gfx1201)"]
    COMM["Comm: NCCL/RCCL, P2P one-shot all-reduce"]
  end
  OAI & ANT & UI --> TOK --> SCH
  SCH <--> KV
  SCH --> SPEC --> PLAN
  SCH --> PLAN --> KR --> CUDA & HIP & CPU
  PLAN --> SMP
  REC --> PLAN
  BLK --> PLAN
  QF --> KR
  PLAN --> COMM
  Core -. events .-> MET
  MET --> UI
```

**Status (section 2 diagram).** Boxes that are **planned** or **partial**: `KV` ("paged blocks, radix prefix cache, host tier"; partial: live KV is contiguous per slot ([`state.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/state.rs)); the opt-in content-addressed prefix store keeps paged, content-addressed prefix states in device, host and disk tiers ([`prefix_store.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/prefix_store.rs)); there is no radix tree), `SPEC` (partial: n-gram (Metal only) and MTP (CUDA, HIP, Metal; one sequence) are in, see [`spec.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/spec.rs) and [`model/spec_graph.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/model/spec_graph.rs); no DFlash drafter), `QF` (partial: no GGUF k-quants, AWQ/GPTQ), `BLK` (partial: sliding window exists only inside the Gemma 4 block, [`model/gemma.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/model/gemma.rs); no MLA, no Mamba2), `KR` "autotune DB" (planned), `HIP` and `CUDA` are implemented, `COMM` "NCCL/RCCL" (partial: NCCL on CUDA and a 2-rank P2P one-shot all-reduce on HIP, no RCCL), "OTLP" in `MET` (planned), `/v1/responses` in `OAI` (planned), `PLAN` "captured graphs per batch bucket" (partial: graphs are captured per decode row count, not per rounded bucket, see 3.6). Metal ([`crates/intarsia-backend-metal`](../crates/intarsia-backend-metal)) is implemented but missing from the diagram's `HW` subgraph. The picture in [architecture-diagram.md](architecture-diagram.md) marks planned components with dashed outlines.

---

## 3. Core abstractions (the pieces)

### 3.1 Backend trait (minimal on purpose)

```rust
pub trait Backend: Send + Sync {
    fn info(&self) -> DeviceInfo;                       // arch, mem, bandwidth (measured), features
    fn alloc(&self, bytes: usize, kind: MemKind) -> Result<Buffer>;
    fn copy(&self, dst: &Buffer, src: &Buffer, stream: StreamId) -> Result<()>;
    fn launch(&self, k: &LoadedKernel, args: &KernelArgs, stream: StreamId) -> Result<()>;
    fn graph_begin(&self, stream: StreamId) -> Result<()>;
    fn graph_end(&self, stream: StreamId) -> Result<GraphHandle>;
    fn graph_replay(&self, g: &GraphHandle, stream: StreamId) -> Result<()>;
    fn event(&self, stream: StreamId) -> Result<Event>;
    fn comm(&self) -> Option<&dyn Comm>;                 // TP collectives
}
```


**Status (3.1).**

| Claim | Status | Evidence on origin/main |
|---|---|---|
| A minimal `Backend` trait is the whole device contract | **partial** | [`backend.rs:192`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/backend.rs): the trait exists with 33 methods, 9 required (`name`, `info`, `alloc`, `upload`, `download`, `copy`, `kernels`, `launch`, `synchronize`); the rest have defaults. Shape differs from the sketch: `launch` is `launch(kernel_name, &OpCall, stream)`, graphs are `graph_capture`/`graph_replay`, there is no `event` |
| `fn comm(&self) -> Option<&dyn Comm>` | **partial** | no `comm` method on the trait; TP collectives are built from backend lists in [`crates/intarsia-core/src/comm.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/comm.rs) and per-backend files |
| Everything above the trait is backend-neutral | **partial** | backend-specific branches remain: [`crates/intarsia-core/src/model/batch.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/model/batch.rs) tests `backend.name() != "cpu"`, and `--max-batch` above 1 is refused on any backend but Metal, CUDA and HIP (and the CPU backend with `INTARSIA_RECURRENT_BATCH=1`) in [`crates/intarsia-models/src/load.rs`](../crates/intarsia-models/src/load.rs) |
| A Vulkan or SYCL backend only has to implement the trait plus its kernel packs | **planned** | no such backend; `kernels/abi/ik_abi.h` takes a CUDA-stream-shaped `void* stream` and CUDA/HIP share `ik_*` symbol names |
| Backend init applies known-bad-default fixes as data (`GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1`) | **partial** | applied by the launchers, not by backend init: [`crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/onboard.rs`](../crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/onboard.rs), [`crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/qualify.rs`](../crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/qualify.rs); `doctor` only reports it ([`crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/doctor.rs`](../crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/doctor.rs)) |


Everything else (ops, quant, attention) lives above the trait. A Vulkan or SYCL backend for Arc only has to implement this plus its kernel packs. Backend init applies known-bad-default fixes as data (for example `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` on HIP, which removed a permanent 20% slowdown).

### 3.2 Kernel registry: the core of modularity and accuracy

Every **op** (e.g. `matmul`, `rmsnorm_add`, `rope`, `paged_attn_decode`, `paged_attn_verify`, `moe_gate_topk`, `moe_grouped_gemm`, `all_reduce_norm_quant`) has:

1. A **signature**: typed inputs/outputs, layouts, quant format.
2. A **reference implementation** in `cpu-ref` (f32/f64 accumulate). This is the oracle.
3. Any number of **implementations**, each declaring `(backend, arch set, dtype/quant, shape predicate, exactness class)`.

```rust
register_kernel! {
    op: Matmul, name: "nvfp4_gemv_splitk_v1",
    backend: Cuda, arch: [sm_121], weights: Nvfp4, acts: [Bf16, Fp8E4m3],
    when: |s| s.m <= 8 && s.k % 64 == 0,          // shape preconditions are code, checked at plan time
    exact: Exactness::Deterministic,               // or BitExactVsSerial / Tolerance(...)
    tol: Tol { max_abs: 2e-2, rel_l2: 5e-3 },
}
```

Rules:
- **Admission test**: `intarsia kernels test` runs every registered implementation against its reference over a shape sweep (including the recipe's real shapes) and records pass/fail plus error stats. A kernel that fails is unselectable on that host. This catches the "compiles for sm_120 but runs garbage on sm_121" class.
- **Plan-time preconditions**: shape predicates are evaluated when the plan is built, so traps like "MXFP4 GEMM needs per-rank K % 128" fail loudly at load, not as token-0 output.
- **Autotuner**: for each (op, shape bucket) on a host, time the eligible implementations and store the winner in a **tuning DB** keyed by host fingerprint (GPU, driver, toolkit, kernel-pack hash). The DB is a committed lockfile per platform (`tuning/<fingerprint>.toml`) so results reproduce.
- **Exactness modes** (from TensorFold): `fast` (any passing kernel), `deterministic` (fixed reduction order, run-to-run identical), `exact` (multi-row verify equals serial decode bit-for-bit; required for lossless speculation claims). Mode is a server flag and is reported in every result.


**Status (3.2).**

| Claim | Status | Evidence on origin/main |
|---|---|---|
| Every op has a typed signature | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-core/src/ops.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/ops.rs): `Op` enum, 42 ops with arity and shape checks. The example op names (`paged_attn_decode`, `paged_attn_verify`, `moe_gate_topk`, `moe_grouped_gemm`, `all_reduce_norm_quant`) are plan names; the real ones are `AttnDecode`, `AttnPrefill`, `MoeTopk`, `MoeExperts`, `MoeBlock`, and there is no all-reduce op |
| Reference implementation per op in `cpu-ref` | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-backend-cpu/src/reference.rs`](../crates/intarsia-backend-cpu/src/reference.rs) |
| Many implementations per op, each with (backend, arch, dtype/quant, shape predicate, exactness) | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-core/src/registry.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/registry.rs) `KernelImpl` |
| `register_kernel!` macro | **partial** | [`registry.rs:247`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/registry.rs) defines it; only that file uses it. Backends build `KernelImpl` values directly ([`crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/src/kernels.rs`](../crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/src/kernels.rs)). The `tol:` field in the example is illustrative |
| Admission test, `intarsia kernels test`; failing kernel is unselectable | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-core/src/admission.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/admission.rs), [`crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/kernels.rs`](../crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/kernels.rs) |
| Plan-time preconditions fail loudly at load | **implemented** | [`crates/intarsia-core/src/plan.rs`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/plan.rs) returns `Error::NoKernel` when no admitted kernel fits |
| Autotuner and tuning DB committed as `tuning/<fingerprint>.toml` | **planned** | no autotuner code and no `tuning/` directory; selection is static priority among admitted kernels |
| Exactness modes `fast`, `deterministic`, `exact` | **implemented** | [`registry.rs:16`](../crates/intarsia-core/src/registry.rs) `Exactness` enum, shown by `intarsia kernels` |
| Mode is a server flag reported in every result | **planned** | no `--exactness` flag in `serve` or `common.rs`; exactness is a per-kernel tag |

### 3.3 Kernel ABI and kernel packs

Every pack is a **port**, not an import (most upstream kernels take `torch::Tensor`). The port target is one torch-free C ABI, `kernels/abi/ik_abi.h`:

```c
typedef struct { void* data; int32_t dtype; int32_t ndim; int64_t shape[6]; int64_t stride[6]; } ik_tensor;
typedef struct { const void* scales; const void* zeros; int32_t group; int32_t format; } ik_quant;
// every launcher: raw tensors in, status out, explicit stream, no allocation inside
int ik_rmsnorm_add(const ik_tensor* x, const ik_tensor* res, const ik_tensor* w, float eps, ik_tensor* out, void* stream);
```

Kernels are compiled by `nvcc`/`hipcc` into a static library per backend and bound from Rust via `extern "C"`. The same shim pattern covers HIP, where Rust bindings are thin (no RCCL or hipBLASLt crates).

| Pack | Backend | License | Port first |
|---|---|---|---|
| `native` (ours) | CUDA + HIP | Apache-2.0 | norms, rope, embedding, sampling, simple attention, glue |
| `tensorfold` | CUDA (+ its ROCm variants) | MIT | EXL3 linear/experts, NVFP4 `qmmf`, GDN, DFlash verify, attention: holds the Spark bar |
| `radiance` (`libr4d`) | HIP gfx1201 | Apache-2.0 (keep `NOTICE`) | MXFP4×FP8 GEMM, one-shot 2/3-rank all-reduce (+norm+quant), GDN recurrent update, paged attention, int2 lm_head: holds the R9700 bar |
| `cublaslt` / `hipblaslt` | vendor | vendor | prefill GEMM, registered as `Exactness::Fast` only (algorithm choice varies by shape; graphs freeze one) |

Other packs (flashinfer, cutlass, ggml, exl3 upstream, ck/aiter) are added only when a measured gap names one. Rule: **no pack is vendored without its license file in `LICENSES/`**, pinned by commit, and every exported kernel passes the admission test.

**Block-scope fused ops are first-class.** Radiance and TensorFold are fast because of hand-fused, family-specific kernels (all-reduce in a GEMV epilogue, norm+quant into GDN). A generic pattern-rewriting fuser is a compiler project we will not build. Instead the registry holds fused block ops (e.g. `gdn_layer_decode_fused`, `attn_block_decode_fused`, `all_reduce_rmsnorm_fp8`) whose reference is the generic op chain. The plan compiler picks the fused op when one is admitted for the shape, else falls back to the chain.


**Status (3.3).**

| Claim | Status | Evidence on origin/main |
|---|---|---|
| One torch-free C ABI, `kernels/abi/ik_abi.h` | **implemented** | [`kernels/abi/ik_abi.h`](../kernels/abi/ik_abi.h) (`ik_tensor`, `ik_quant`; launcher comment still says Phase 0 dense BF16) |

name: prose-4k-2
input:
Here are some notes I have been collecting, just for background mood and vocabulary.

| `fp8_act` | string | `"static"` | FP8 checkpoints: `"static"` quantises activations with the checkpoint's `input_scale` (W8A8), `"none"` keeps them 16-bit (W8A16). No effect on other formats. See [quant-moe.md](quant-moe.md). Override with `--fp8-act`. |
| `w4a4_as_w4a16` | bool | `false` | A checkpoint that declares plain `NVFP4` (weights AND 4-bit activations, W4A4) is refused by the loader (`Gemma4` layers) and not covered by the recipe in `recipe new` / `onboard`, because the engine runs NVFP4 weight-only (W4A16): a deviation from the declared scheme and from vLLM. `true` accepts that knowingly (Gemma-4 NVFP4 does). |
| `mxfp4_act` | string | unset (what the checkpoint declares) | MXFP4 checkpoints: `"dynamic"` runs the W4A4 a Quark checkpoint declares (dynamic MXFP4 activations), `"none"` keeps activations 16-bit (W4A16), `"fp8"` quantises each token's activations to fp8 e4m3 (W4A8; HIP only, other backends refuse it at load with a message). Precedence: `--mxfp4-act`, then `[tuning.<backend>] mxfp4_act`, then this key, then the checkpoint's declaration. No effect on a checkpoint without MXFP4 projections. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets `"none"` (the Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4: full MMLU n=1425 W4A16 0.822 vs W4A4 0.802, `docs/results/2026-10-27-act27-27b-w4a16-mmlu.md`; cost at tp2: prefill -30%, decode -13..-19%); `--mxfp4-act dynamic` runs the declared W4A4. The same file overrides it on HIP with `[tuning.hip] mxfp4_act = "fp8"`, so CUDA and Metal keep W4A16. |

### `[tuning]` and `[tuning.<backend>]`

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prefill_chunk` | int, at least 1 | `256` (code default) | Tokens per prefill forward pass, for every backend. Override with `--prefill-chunk`. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] prefill_chunk` | int, at least 1 | the base value | Same, for one backend: `cpu`, `cuda`, `hip` or `metal`. A backend without a table uses the base value. |
| `mtp_draft_vocab` | int, multiple of 8 | `0` (the full head) | Default of `--mtp-draft-vocab` for every backend: the MTP drafter's argmax runs over the first N `lm_head` rows. Output is unchanged (the verify pass keeps the full head); only acceptance moves. `0` or unset: the full head. Set only where measured. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mtp_draft_vocab` | int, multiple of 8 | the base value | Same, for one backend. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` (Qwen3.8-27B) sets `[tuning.hip] mtp_draft_vocab = 65536`; CUDA and Metal are unmeasured and keep the full head. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mtp_default_tp_k` | int > 0 | unset (off) | With in-process tensor parallelism (`--tp N`, N > 1) on that backend, one sequence and no `--spec` given: run `--spec mtp --spec-k K` (a lone `--spec-k N` without `--spec` keeps this default with k = N; where no default applies it warns and speculation stays off). Needs `[mtp]` and a dense MTP head in the checkpoint (else plain decode with a note). `--spec off` or `INTARSIA_SPEC_DEFAULT=0` opts out; a configured prefix store (`--prefix-store`, `INTARSIA_PREFIX_STORE`) skips the default with one line (a drafting request bypasses the store). Per backend only (lane dfh, docs/results/2026-10-26-dfh-hip-dflash.md). |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mxfp4_act` | string | unset (the `[defaults]` value) | MXFP4 checkpoints: the activation mode on that backend when `--mxfp4-act` is not given (`"dynamic"`, `"none"` or `"fp8"`, as in `[defaults] mxfp4_act`). For a mode only some backends implement: `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets `"fp8"` under `[tuning.hip]` (W4A8: full MMLU n=1425 0.8204 vs W4A16 0.822; against W4A16 at tp2 prefill +48%, decode +11%; KL to the W4A16 golden 12x below W4A4's; `docs/results/2026-10-27-w4a8-hip-fp8-act.md`). A backend with no kernels for the mode refuses an explicit `--mxfp4-act fp8` at load. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mtp_default_k` | int > 0 | unset (off) | With one rank (no `--tp`) on that backend, one sequence and no `--spec` given: run `--spec mtp --spec-k K` (a lone `--spec-k N` without `--spec` keeps this default with k = N). Needs `[mtp]` and the MTP head in the checkpoint (else plain decode with a note). `--spec off` or `INTARSIA_SPEC_DEFAULT=0` opts out; `--max-batch` above 1 keeps plain decode; a configured prefix store (`--prefix-store`, `INTARSIA_PREFIX_STORE`) skips the default with one line. Set for the Qwen3.6-35B on CUDA (`recipes/qwen3_5_moe.toml`, `mtp_default_k = 2`): decode 1.17-1.5x per category, prefill within 1 % of `--spec off` (lane mpf, docs/results/2026-10-27-mpf-macro-prefill-mtp.md), and for the Qwen3.8-27B on CUDA (`recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` `[tuning.cuda]`, with `mtp_draft_vocab = 65536`): decode x1.70 at 1k, prefill unchanged (lane s27d, docs/results/2026-10-27-s27d-cuda-27b-decode.md). |
| `[tuning.<backend>] busy_chunk` | int >= 1 | unset (the loader's rule: the model's prefill chunk for the batched recurrent models, else 256) | Rows of a prefill chunk that runs beside decoding sequences under `serve --max-batch` > 1, on that backend; `--busy-chunk` wins, and the engine clamps it to the model chunk. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets 256 on HIP next to `prefill_chunk = 2048`: a request alone prefills in 2048-row chunks, one arriving beside decoding streams in 256-row chunks, so their per-token stall stays at 135 ms (a 2048-row chunk stalls them 650 ms). |
| `[tuning.<backend>] tp_partial` | `"f32"` or `"bf16"` | unset (`f32`) | Tensor parallelism (`--tp N`, N > 1) on that backend: the dtype of the row-parallel partials (attention o, FFN down, GatedDeltaNet out) the all-reduce sums. `f32`: each rank keeps its partial in f32 and the sum is rounded to bf16 once, as one unsharded matmul would; `bf16`: each rank rounds its partial to bf16 and the all-reduce sums in place (half the bytes, two roundings per reduce). `INTARSIA_TP_PARTIAL=f32\|bf16` wins over the recipe. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets `"bf16"` under `[tuning.hip]` (Qwen3.8-27B at tp2 on the R9700s: prefill +17 % at 1k / 4k / 16k, MMLU n=1425 0.8218 against 0.8204, `docs/results/2026-10-27-tpb-hip-tp-partials.md`); every other backend and model keeps `f32`. Greedy ids differ from the f32 partials' ids. |
| `prefill_peel`, `[tuning.<backend>] prefill_peel` | int, 0..255 | `0` (off) | Prefill tail peel in rows: a forward pass longer than 256 rows whose length mod 256 is 1..=N runs those last rows as their own pass, as the default 256-row schedule cuts them, so a larger chunk gives the default chunk's bits where every kernel is row-invariant above N rows (`crates/intarsia-core/src/scheduler.rs` `peel_tail`). Same resolution as `prefill_chunk`; `INTARSIA_PREFILL_PEEL` overrides it. No builtin recipe sets it: for Qwen3.8-27B on HIP, `--prefill-chunk 4096` with `INTARSIA_PREFILL_PEEL=16` is bitwise chunk 256 and +35-43 % prefill, but under `serve --max-batch 16` it costs context and runs 4096-row busy chunks (docs/results/2026-10-25-mx-hip-27b-prefill.md section 4). |

Here are some notes I have been collecting, just for background mood and vocabulary. flags, and the output line `SELF-STATS ...` the acceptance script reads: | check | flag | default | |---|---|---| | mean 21-way KL(old \|\| new) | `--self-max-kl` | 1e-4 | | largest single-position 21-way KL | `--self-max-pos-kl` | 5e-3 | | top-1 flips, percent of positions (at least one position) | `--self-max-flip-pct` | 0.5 | | mean per-position `\|tail difference\|` | `--self-max-tail` | 5e-4 | | worst prompt's mean KL | `--self-prompt-factor` x `--self-max-kl` | 5 x | | non-finite rows | | none | `--self-golden` needs the same model, backend, KV and activation dtype, fp8 mode, prefill chunk and decode positions (`--allow-config-mismatch` to downgrade). It cannot be combined with `--golden`, `--baseline`, `--write-baseline` or `--mode reuse`. `--self-vs-ref-noise` swaps the budgets for the reference-noise rule ("Reference noise" above). ### Choosing the self-golden budgets **Method.** The question a budget answers is "how far does a legitimate change move the logits, and how far a bug". The prompt asked for the budget to come from the run-to-run noise of one build on the Mac cpu backend with Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B. Measured 2026-10-13 (golden `qwen3-reranker-0.6b-long`, 10 prompts, 1434 prefill and 160 decode positions, old build = 4963b43 + harness overlay writing the dump, new build = this tree reading it): | run against the old build's dump | prefill mean KL21 / flips of 1434 | decode mean KL21 / flips of 160 | |---|---|---| | new build, same flags (run-to-run) | 2.5e-14 / 0 | 1.5e-14 / 0 | | `--prefill-chunk 64`, `1024`; `--kv-dtype f32` | identical to the row above (bitwise) | identical | | `--kv-dtype f16` | 2.7e-4 / 19 | 4.7e-4 / 2 | | `--reference` (f64 oracle kernels) | 1.3e-3 / 26 | 1.1e-3 / 2 | 1. **Run-to-run noise on one build is exactly zero** (1e-14 is the f32 rounding of the stored log-probs): the engine is bit-reproducible on the cpu, so no budget can be derived from it, and a budget set as a multiple of it would reject any legitimate reordering. (On GPU it is probably also zero; the acceptance script checks it: the new build against its own dump from a second process, budgets 1e-9 / 1e-6 / 0 flips.) 2. **The smallest non-zero perturbation already saturates this model.** `INTARSIA_CPU_FAULT=:

` (`crates/intarsia-backend-cpu/src/fault.rs`, off by default, for gate-sensitivity checks only) moves each bf16 output element of the named ops one ulp up or down with probability `p`, the output change a kernel with another summation order produces. `p = 4.7e-3` is rel_l2 3.5e-4, the size measured between the old and the grouped MoE kernel (unit test `flip_rate_to_rel_l2`); rel_l2 is about `5.1e-3 * sqrt(p)`. | `matmul` flip rate p (rel_l2 of each matmul output) | prefill mean KL21 / flips | decode mean KL21 / flips | |---|---|---| | 1e-9 (a handful of flips in about 1e9 outputs) | 9.2e-4 / 24 | 4.9e-4 / 2 | | 1e-6 | 1.0e-3 / 27 | 1.1e-3 / 2 | | 1e-4 | 1.3e-3 / 31 | 1.2e-3 / 3 | | 4.7e-3 (3.5e-4) | 1.2e-3 / 27 | 9.2e-4 / 3 | | 2e-2 (7e-4) | 1.4e-3 / 33 | 1.2e-3 / 3 | | 0.2 (2.3e-3) | 2.0e-3 / 45 | 1.8e-3 / 1 | | 1.0 (5.1e-3) | 3.6e-3 / 50 | 3.8e-3 / 4 | | attention only, p = 1 | 1.4e-3 / 32 | 1.3e-3 / 3 | One flipped ulp in the long prompts moves the whole prompt's KL by about 1e-3: the response is flat from a handful of flips up to rel_l2 1e-3 and only then grows (the 0.6B reranker's distributions are flat and an early token's change propagates to every later position). **On this model the noise floor of any non-zero change is about 1e-3 mean KL and 2% top-1 flips**, ten times the review's 1e-4 target. The Mac proxy therefore cannot calibrate a 35B budget (sharper distributions, NVFP4 weights, 40 layers of MoE): it only shows the shape of the problem. 3. **What the budget must do is decided on the target model**, so the defaults are the review's targets (1e-4 / 5e-3 / 0.5% / 5e-4, prompt x5) and the acceptance run derives the budgets it applies as `max(default, 3 x floor)`, where the floor is measured in the same run on the real weights: the pre-change build against its own dump with the SIMT attention kernels instead of flash / split-KV (`INTARSIA_CUDA_DISABLE=attn_decode_bf16_splitkv,attn_prefill_bf16_splitkv,attn_prefill_bf16_flash`), a numerically equivalent reordering. If the floor is above the defaults the gate is less sensitive on that model and the log says by how much; if it is below, the defaults apply. The rule is fixed in the script header before any number exists. **Sensitivity check (the gate can see a change the old gates cannot).** Old build baseline `B0` and dump `S0`, new build with `INTARSIA_CPU_FAULT=matmul:1e-9` (about one flipped element in 1e9 matmul outputs): the baseline gate (floor, baseline, per prompt) PASSES (KL against HF moves from 2.380e-3 to 2.463e-3 prefill, within x1.15) while the self-golden gate FAILS (mean KL21 9.2e-4 against 1e-4). With `matmul:4.7e-3` (a legitimate-size reordering of every matmul) the baseline gate passes with the shipped margins and fails at `matmul:2e-2` (rel_l2 7e-4) on the per-prompt KL, the quantity the old aggregate gate could not see. Those margins (x2.5 max KL, x1.75 per prompt) are the ones that separate the two on this model; they were x1.5 / x1.3 in the first draft and failed the legitimate-size case. They are untested on the 35B. ### TP self-golden budget (tp=2 against tp=1): measured, not shipped **Question.** `--tp 2` against a `--tp 1` self-golden of the same weights (Qwen3-8B BF16, 2x R9700) fails the default budgets by 5-6x (mean KL 5.9e-4 prefill, 5.1e-4 decode against 1e-4). Is that a defect, or the size of an equally correct reordering, and can a TP budget be derived from measured noise rather than set by hand? **Method** (all on the long fp32 prompt set, 10 prompts, 1434 prefill and 160 decode positions; raw logs in `docs/results/2026-10-14-tp2-budget-logs/`, table generator `scripts/tp2-budget-summarize.py`, results `docs/results/2026-10-14-tp2-budget.md`). `S0` is the tp=1 default dump. Every other configuration is run against `S0` with the default budget flags, and only its `SELF-STATS` line is read. 1. **Spread of equivalent tp=1 variants against `S0`**: run twice (second process), device 1 instead of 0, `INTARSIA_NO_FUSION=1`, `--prefill-chunk 1024`, `--prefill-chunk 64`, `INTARSIA_HIP_DISABLE` of the flash / split-KV attention kernels (SIMT attention), of the decode gemv kernels (`matmul_bf16_gemv,logits_bf16_gemv`), and the combination. Run-to-run, device 1, `INTARSIA_NO_FUSION=1` (the run reports the same resolved kernels: the fused kernels do not apply to this model, so fusion is not a difference between tp=1 and tp=2 here) and chunk 1024 (2 of 10 prompts span more than one chunk of 256, none of 1024) are bitwise identical to `S0` (mean KL 9e-11, the rounding of the stored log-probs). The variants that move the logits are SIMT attention, the gemv switch and, a little, chunk 64: | tp=1 variant vs `S0` | prefill mean KL / max pos KL / flips of 1434 / tail / worst prompt | decode mean KL / max pos KL / flips of 160 / tail / worst prompt | |---|---|---| | chunk 64 | 1.2e-6 / 3.3e-4 / 0 / 5.2e-7 / 2.0e-5 | 4.7e-5 / 2.9e-3 / 0 / 3.6e-6 / 4.7e-4 | | SIMT attention (= with no-fusion, chunk 64) | **6.07e-4 / 4.9e-2 / 6** / 1.6e-4 / 7.7e-4 | **3.54e-4** / 6.2e-3 / 0 / 2.0e-4 / 7.6e-4 | | decode gemv off | 9e-11 (identical) | 2.89e-4 / **8.9e-3** / 0 / **2.1e-4** / **1.15e-3** | | **max over the variants** | 6.07e-4 / 4.9e-2 / 6 (0.42%) | 3.54e-4 / 8.9e-3 / 0 / 2.1e-4 / 1.15e-3 | 2. **tp=2 against `S0`** (f32 partials, P2P): prefill 5.90e-4 / 5.0e-2 / 5 flips / 1.5e-4 / 9.8e-4, decode 5.07e-4 / 1.5e-2 / 0 / 2.1e-4 / 2.0e-3. The P2P and host communicators, and a second run, give the same numbers to the last digit; bf16 partials, chunk 64 and SIMT attention under tp=2 land at 5.6-5.9e-4 prefill (5-7 flips) and 3.8-5.1e-4 decode. 3. **Distance to the fp32 golden** (what the floor measures; full-vocabulary KL, prefill / decode): tp=1 variants 3.97e-4 - 4.22e-4 / 2.70e-4 - 3.57e-4, tp=2 4.19e-4 / 3.45e-4: **inside the spread of the tp=1 variants**. The top-1 agreement is 99.51% for tp=2 against 99.58% for every tp=1 variant (one position; the tp=2 variants span 99.51 - 99.86%). On the short golden's prompts (434 / 128 positions) tp=2 (3.90e-4 prefill) is outside the three tp=1 runs there (2.34e-4 - 3.28e-4); the budget below was derived on the long set only. 4. **Conclusion on the numbers**: tp=2 against tp=1 is the same kind of perturbation as the attention-kernel switch. The prefill figures are inside the tp=1 spread, the decode figures (5.1e-4 against 3.5e-4) outside it by 1.4x and inside it at k = 2. The default 1e-4 budget was chosen for single-kernel changes and cannot apply to TP. **Derived TP budget** (budget = max over the tp=1 variants x k, with k = 2 = `envelope::DEFAULT_K`, not touched): | check | max over tp=1 variants (which) | x 2 | tp=2 observed | |---|---|---|---| | mean 21-way KL | 6.07e-4 (SIMT attention, prefill) | 1.2e-3 | 5.9e-4 / 5.1e-4 | | largest single-position KL | 4.9e-2 (SIMT attention, prefill) | 9.8e-2 | 5.0e-2 / 1.5e-2 | | top-1 flips (prefill) | 6 of 1434 (SIMT attention) | 12 = 0.84% | 5 | | mean \|tail diff\| | 2.1e-4 (gemv off, decode) | 4.2e-4 | 1.5e-4 / 2.1e-4 | | worst prompt mean KL | 1.15e-3 (gemv off, decode) | 2.3e-3 (x1.9 the mean-KL budget) | 9.8e-4 / 2.0e-3 | tp=2 passes all five with margin (the tightest, worst prompt in decode, at 86% of its limit). **It was not shipped, because it does not catch a 1% partial-scale bug.** `INTARSIA_TP_TEST_BUG=scale:F[@RANK]` (test-only, `crates/intarsia-core/src/model.rs`; printed in the self-golden's exec diff as a fault) multiplies one rank's partial by `F` before every all-reduce (rank 1 by default). The derived budget fails the rank-1 realisation on a single heavy-tailed statistic (the largest KL of 1434 positions; it also fails a 0.1% bug, and reads 1.6e-1 for clean tp=2 with bf16 partials against the tp=2 default dump) and passes the rank-0 realisation and the short golden's prompts. The mean KL, flips and worst-prompt checks only see the bug from 2% (long golden; on the short golden's 128 decode positions it fails at 2% by 1.23e-3 against 1.21e-3) or 3%. No single mean-KL budget separates a 1% bug from clean tp=2 either: the rank-0 bug's decode figure (5.8e-4) is below clean tp=2's prefill figure (5.9e-4), and its prefill figure (7.4e-4) is 1.2x the SIMT-attention spread, k = 1.2 instead of the envelope's 2. **What guards TP instead.** (a) the Mac f32 test `tp2_matches_tp1_prefill_and_decode_f32` (`crates/intarsia-models/tests/tp.rs`, summation order 2.5e-7 against its 1e-5 bound) and `tp_test_bug.rs` (the same comparison with `scale:1.01` gives 5.7e-3: 23000x the clean figure): it checks the sharding and the reduction exactly, in `cargo test --workspace`; (b) the exact all-reduce tests on the GPU (`crates/intarsia-backend-hip/tests/comm.rs`); (c) the fp32-golden floor on both prompt sets (`--gate-class bf16`), which fails a partial-scale bug from 2%. A tp=2 run that fails it while passing the vLLM `--ref-noise` gate is not a failure. It is slow; use it on short goldens, or with `--decode-positions`.
